title: Fogg's day, by the clock — enter Passepartout
learning_goal: Know Fogg's timetable and who Passepartout is; feel precision as comedy and like the valet at once.

narration.script: Fogg's day, by the clock. Tap any line to see what happens. He rises at eight. Tea and toast at twenty-three minutes past. Shaving-water at nine thirty-seven, at thirty degrees — eighty-six Fahrenheit. Out of the door at half past eleven, home at midnight. Into this house, at twenty-nine minutes past eleven, walks Passepartout: a Parisian of Paris, about thirty. Once a wandering singer, then a circus-rider who vaulted like Léotard, a rope-dancer like Blondin. Then a fireman in Paris, then ten English households in five years. He wants a quiet life. Look at his face on the card; we like him already — the man with the slow watch.

media.note: REQUESTED (Content Preparer): typeset card in the style of a Victorian railway timetable, six rows (8:00, 8:23, 9:37, 11:29, 11:30, 12:00), each tappable. No illustration budget needed.

interaction.prompt: Tap a time on Fogg's timetable.

options.feedback: Every day the same minute. The house is lit and warmed by gas, with electric bells and speaking-tubes to call the valet.
Twenty-three minutes past eight, not a minute later. Wardrobe items are numbered by season, so nothing needs deciding.
About 30 °C — Verne says 86 °F. This morning James Forster brought it two degrees cold, and was dismissed for it. That is why there is a vacancy.
'Twenty-nine minutes after eleven, a.m., this Wednesday, 2nd October' — Passepartout is engaged. His watch, Fogg notes, is four minutes slow.
Fogg leaves for the Reform Club at half past eleven sharp. Passepartout's first words alone in the house are the Tussaud's line on the caption.
Home at midnight, every night. Passepartout has served in ten English houses in five years; this one, he thinks, will finally be quiet.

transition.music_cue: none; a soft clock tick under the card is allowed

production_notes: Temperature conversion is arithmetic on F-02 (86 °F ≈ 30 °C), metric first per style guide. The guide reads only the times and the CV; the taps hold the punchlines (the 84 °F sacking, the four-minutes-slow watch, the Tussaud's line) — pause_narration: each tap pauses the guide for its feedback, timeout_s 12 per tap. Passepartout's Tussaud's line keeps Verne's exclamation mark on the caption, attributed; the guide never reads it aloud. Narrator: break the CV after 'about thirty' and after 'Blondin' (done roughly here), end on the noun. Linear cut: card only, no taps, 40 s — script trimmed after 'home at midnight' to the one-breath CV.
